quote: TC Pressure is at the turbocharger. MAP is at the manifold. They're absolute
author: ktuner

claim: On a 10th gen CVT, a damaged PRL catted downpipe (loose cat flaking) caused extreme rich trims (STFT/LTFT maxed, P0172); after stock parts and a replacement downpipe, LTFT returned to 0 +/-2%.
quote: Looks like the damaged downpipe was indeed the issue.
author: coupe-r

claim: KTuner staff confirmed work on updating existing maps for the 2018 oil dilution recall.
quote: Yes
author: ktuner

claim: KTuner only flashes the ECU; the newer ECU software requires the CVT module software update, which only Honda or a shop with flashing capability can do.
quote: We only flash the ECU, which is the issue with the version change.
author: ktuner

claim: Throttle response: KTuner says Sport mode affects ECU internals and other modules so it will always feel sharper than Normal even with max throttle response; the pedal is never 1:1 because the plate is opened to help spool the turbo; drivability options are global.
quote: It never will, as by design it opens the plate to help spool the turbo etc.
author: ktuner

claim: KTuner staff: low-throttle spool is slow on a 1.5L; you can ramp boost in slowly to soften the feel.
quote: You can always ramp boost in slowly!
author: ktuner

claim: A Hondata-to-KTuner non-Si CVT owner ran aggressive KTuner variations for 1.5 years with no issues; PRL CAI with Race MAF needs the Race MAF setting in the tune.
quote: got the PRL CAI w/ Race MAF tuned w/ Race MAF setting and continue to have no issues.
author: smokeelaa

claim: KTuner staff: the Honda ECU is a target-torque based system, not target boost, so peak boost varies with elevation and other factors.
quote: it is a target torque based system, not target boost.
author: ktuner

claim: KTuner staff: at altitude (not sea level) the same 17 psi gauge reading already represents more relative pressure; compare tune vs stock in the same conditions.
quote: If you're not at sea level then you're actually boosting more than 17 already, relative pressure.
author: ktuner

claim: KTuner staff: the downpipe tune changes CAM angle commands compared with the non-downpipe tune.
quote: CAM angle commands are changed in the DP tune.
author: ktuner

claim: Knock Control (K.Con) rising to .85 does not mean engine damage: higher numbers mean timing is retarded so less power; it depends on octane, IAT and load. Normal cruise on 93 octane stays ~.49; 91 octane at 21 psi also ~.49.
quote: Higher numbers mean timing is getting retarded so you have less power.
author: gtman

claim: An owner saw K.Con jump to ~.87 in slow traffic when IAT was 90F+ and fuel quality was poor, versus never above .55 in cooler weather.
quote: Now that my IAT is easily 90°+ I get these random high jumps in knock
author: cvcturbo

claim: KTuner staff: KTuner can log G-force with extended logging enabled; torque/power can be estimated from MAF g/s.
quote: Some posts online suggest calculating torque/power by using MAF g/sec.
author: ktuner

claim: KTuner staff do not recommend vent-to-atmosphere BOVs (MAF is upstream of the turbo so venting disturbs metering).
quote: We don't recommend a vent to atmosphere BOV
author: ktuner

claim: Idle speed is an option under Main Parameters in KTuner; throttle response and other drivability settings are global across the three on-the-fly maps because high boost targets open the throttle plate near fully even at half pedal; lower targets and responsiveness settings to make it gentler.
quote: Idle is an option under main parameters.
author: ktuner

claim: KTuner staff (Mar 2019): over 5000 active 1.5T Civics worldwide were running KTuner tunes; 50 failures would be a 1% rate.
quote: totaling over 5000 active 1.5T Civics around the world currently utilizing the software.
author: ktuner

claim: Non-Si stock peak boost is roughly 12-13 psi; first KTuner base map (16.5 psi) already adds boost; Starter 21 is about 8 psi over stock.
quote: the actual boost you hit stock on a non si is around 12-13 psi
author: dallasjhawk

claim: Tuned CVT Civic owner: after a year, drivability and turbo lag improve most, mpg similar if driven gently (40s mpg highway tuned), lower if heavy footed.
quote: On highway drives (driving the speed limit), I've seen MPG's in the 40's, tuned.
author: gtman

claim: Base maps are reported safe: no known blown engine on unaltered base tune on unmodded unabused car; failures usually custom tunes, 2-stepping a cold engine or abuse; clutch is first to fail; stock turbo is cheap to replace.
quote: you'd be hard pressed to find one that blew using an unaltered base tune, on an unmodded, unabused car.
author: gtman

claim: Stock clutch break-in is 600 miles per manual; one owner first flashed a mild basemap at 2500 miles; clutch bedding needs gear changes.
quote: Break-in is 600 miles per your manual.
author: charleswrivers

claim: KTuner staff: final ignition timing is built from multiple tables and seeing about 0 degrees at WOT on a base map is not uncommon (room is left in base maps).
quote: There are multiple tables that go into deciding the final ignition timing values.
author: ktuner

claim: KTuner staff: canned tunes keep torque below the clutch maximum; full boost at low RPM in high gears (lugging) stresses the clutch; limit boost in those gears with Boost By Gear.
quote: Going full boost at low RPM in higher gears, aka lugging the engine, has been known to put extra stress on the clutch.
author: ktuner

claim: OEM clutch results vary: some had no slip for 20,000 miles, others slipped at 1,000 miles; avoid boost in 5th/6th, downshift to pull instead.
quote: some had no clutch slip for 20,000 miles and some slipped at 1,000 miles
author: dc2turbo

claim: There is no psi limit for the stock clutch; it is torque and rpm: one claim ~240 ft-lb +/-10; 300 Nm at 2000 rpm differs from 300 Nm at 3500 rpm; KTuner-side advice: watch for slip and reduce power or change driving.
quote: the stock clutch is good to about 240ish ft lb, give or take 10
author: thatsi

claim: Boost by gear: limit first gear to ~18 psi to stop wheelspin on hot days, TSP Stage 1 also limits 18-19 psi in first; set to a level that does not spin and leave others.
quote: I did a 18# limit in first when I was on the basemaps.
author: charleswrivers

claim: Owner moving from Hondata +6 to KTuner on a CVT found KTuner smoother and with much less lag off the line; enables for spool, throttle response and ramps changed the car character more than boost; Throttle response 1&2 presets cured the sponge feeling on a 2.0 CVT.
quote: The CVT no longer produces a feeling of pushing your foot into a sponge with no result.
author: scallywag502

claim: On a non-Si, boost target cannot be edited in Quick Adjustments; disabling boost ramp and raising part-throttle turbo explains aggressive boost; TunerView showed ~24 psi at 3500-4000 rpm on 21 psi dual starter at 9 ft below sea level in 80F.
quote: Oh you can't even change your boost target on the non-Si in quick adjustments!
author: alexander

claim: KTuner 1.0.8.1 (June 2018) added on-the-fly switching between 3 maps each with separate boost targets and turbo responsiveness; BBG overrides the boost targets and is shared across all three maps (not per map); non-Si support followed.
quote: BBG targets always override standard boost targets.
author: ktuner

claim: KTuner staff: BBG should be set higher than the targets in areas where you do not want BBG to override.
quote: BBG should be higher than the targets in the areas you're not wanting BBG to override.
author: ktuner

claim: Partial Throttle Boost Response was merged into Turbo Responsiveness; Turbo Spool option never existed on Si because it is already aggressive.
quote: Turbo spool was never an option on Si. It's already aggressive.
author: ktuner

claim: KTuner staff: on a stock-boost non-Si many only reached 12-14 psi on the lowest map; ECO still dulls throttle unless quick adjustments are changed; back-to-back testers often get better mileage if they stay out of the throttle; V2 holds factory tune so you can flash back to stock anytime.
quote: Most guys who do test back to back get better mileage with the tune, if they stay out of the gas of course.
author: ktuner

claim: Flashing takes about 3-5 minutes with ignition ON, engine OFF; V2 stores up to 5 maps plus factory; starting from Factory starting point and only changing quick adjustments changes behavior without boost changes.
quote: you have to do it with the ignition on (not ACC.) and the engine off.
author: maddmatt02

claim: KTuner staff: VSA disable reduces VSA module intervention; U0122 disable removes the CAN bus error but also disables the sport mode button; throttle padding is the off/on throttle transition padding used for rev hang disable.
quote: Throttle padding is the padding for off/on throttle transition, used for rev hang disable.
author: ktuner

claim: Cost of the 10th gen setup in the TunerView review: KTuner V1.2 $449, Amazon Fire 7 tablet $50, TunerView app $5.
quote: KTuner V1.2 = $449 Amazon Fire 7 = $50 TunerView = $5
author: kingpinoy

claim: DIFP means Direct Injection Fuel Pressure; abbreviations are listed in the KTuner online help item_abbreviations page (not complete).
quote: DIFP - Direct Injection Fuel Pressure
author: ktuner

claim: LTFT1 does not read -100% unless LTFT2 was selected by mistake (single bank car); STFT1 varying -10% to +15% between accel and cruise is normal-looking.
quote: Long term 1 should not read -100
author: ktuner

claim: KTuner user-adjustable drivability options on the 1.5T: throttle response, turbo response, turbo spool, rev hang, turbo ramp rate, boost targets for normal/sport, boost limits by gear, ignition, fuel targets and ECU function options; KTuner flashes only the ECU.
quote: Throttle response, turbo response, turbo spool, rev hang, turbo ramp rate.
author: ktuner

claim: D-Rob (IMW): Knock Count in KTuner reflects the ECU misfire monitor, not true knock; stock healthy cars accumulate counts at startup, rapid throttle changes, clutch release; only a steep count (50+ in seconds, tripping P0300) is a concern.
quote: It is NOT an accurate reflection of anything other than misfire events.
author: vincent-27won (quoting d-robimw)

claim: D-Rob: Knock Control is the ECU fuel-quality/knock estimate; it is dynamic and moves; on non-Si 1.5T ECUs it rises naturally above 5,200-5,400 rpm regardless of sensor input; worry about values that climb and never come down; it can be pulled down by driving in a higher gear at low rpm near atmospheric MAP.
quote: which naturally rise above 5,200-5,400rpm regardless of sensor input
author: vincent-27won (quoting d-robimw)

claim: D-Rob: Si and non-Si ECU knock sensitivity and knock retard tables are identical above 5,500 rpm; the rise in Knock Control above ~5,200 rpm on stock non-Si cars is a background behavior even when ignition advance is removed.
quote: The knock sensitivity tables on Si (5AM) and non-Si (5AA, 5AN, etc) ECU's are IDENTICAL.
author: d-robimw

claim: Owner reports K.Con of .70-.80 on WOT at 5,000-6,000 rpm in perfect ambient on 92 octane returning to .49 when cruising, consistent with the natural non-Si rise.
quote: But it does go back to .49 when I take it easy again and just cruise
author: jillest

claim: Remedies for K.Con rising under repeated high boost: lower IAT with a bigger intercooler or meth, avoid repeated high-boost high-rpm pulls; sedate driving brings it back down in minutes.
quote: Upgrade the intercooler to lower IAT.
author: micah

claim: Indonesian non-Si CVT owner (RON90, free-flow exhaust, K&N) got knock retard up to 18 and K.Con avg 0.72 at 1250-1500 rpm; fixed with ignition -0.2 in that low-rpm/high-load area, higher fuel-cut delay in gears 3-5, MAF calibration, giving K.Con avg 0.57, STFT avg 0.7%, retard never above 10; later plug gap 0.7 mm and hot-air-intake heat shield made adjustments unnecessary (K.Con .49-.59 normal, .55-.65 aggressive).
quote: Knock Control average 0.57 STFT average 0.7%
author: virhan
ktuner_table_or_setting: Ignition retard, MAF scaling, fuel cut delay

claim: Local fuel octane labeled RON differs from US AKI: RON 92 equals about 88-89 US octane (AKI = (RON+MON)/2).
quote: US Octane rating uses the average of the RON and the MON figures, called the AKI
author: arnoldo

claim: A CVT 10th gen could not reach a 23 psi target: ~20-21 psi max at sea level; logs showed TPS.CMD ~80-90 while TPS at 100, KTuner said cylinder fill limit/mg per stroke and TPS.CMD cap target boost; adjusting the cylinder fill limit table did not fix it; the cause was a KTuner software issue fixed by a beta build (cruise control lost).
quote: The issue was something software related with KTuner.
author: coupe-r

claim: After the fix the car hits 23 psi but overshoots 1-3 psi briefly during the CVT simulated shift at high rpm, which KTuner said is normal.
quote: I do slightly overshoot by 1-3 psi, but it is **only** (emphasize only) for that brief moment
author: coupe-r

claim: Always-aftermarket intake MAF housing matters: 27WON claims its machined MAF housing keeps trims within about 1.5% of OEM intake.
quote: keep the OEM PCM happy
author: vincent-27won

claim: A 2024 Sport Touring 6MT (non-Si 1.5T) on KTuner Starter 21 and TSP Stage 1 had the gas pedal go dead for seconds; clutch-in or shifting restored it; the owner suspects the enabled P0299 underboost monitor in quick adjustments sent the car into limp mode and disabled the monitor.
quote: I had the monitor for P0299 enabled (underboost), which would throw my car into limp mode (dead gas pedal)
author: boostbloofl1

claim: A 2022 Sport Touring hatch CVT on Phearable 1.5 Level 3, 93 octane, aggressive night driving: 6,800 miles tuned with no problems, then 20k tuned miles, then 32k tuned miles at 42k total with no issues, oil every 5k, CVT fluid at 30k.
quote: Just reached 42k miles (32k miles tuned). Have not had any issues whatsoever.
author: maracuch0

claim: 2022 Civic EX CVT on Phearable 1.5 non-Si Map 2 with new intercooler: K.Con steady about 0.47-0.5 and boost targets reached; owner avoids Map 3 to spare the CVT.
quote: K Con. has been steady around 0.47-0.5. Hits boost targets.
author: axion_industries

claim: 2022 Sport Touring CVT on Starter 21 Dual Tune 1 plus throttle/ramp adjustments, 93 octane, 80 mph cruise: no problems and car feels completely different.
quote: the tune made it feel like a completely different vehicle
author: deculture

claim: 2022 EX CVT owner: Starter 21 feels good but Phearable 1.5 is smoother; cruising rarely above 2k rpm; fuel 91 octane + 1.5 gal E85 blend.
quote: The Ktuner starter tunes feel good but the Phearable 1.5 tune feels even better and smoother.
author: sapphire_fe1

claim: Sport Hatch CVT owner on Starter 21 (Stage 2) with 94 octane reports a little CVT whine after long spirited driving.
quote: a little CVT whine after long spirited driving.
author: spitfire

claim: 2022 Civic FE3 owner in China with a custom own tune: 23.5 psi with 7-8 degrees timing advance at about 5500 rpm, 98 octane in mainland China; wonders about 25 psi like TSP Stage 1 map 3.
quote: 23.5psi with 7-8 timing advance at about 5500rpm
author: pangzixin

claim: 2024 Sport Touring 6MT (non-Si 1.5T) owner on Phearable noticed clutch slip at high boost after a summer; backed down to a lower map, then fitted an RV6 FK8 clutch kit; ~36k miles after; early spool on and auto stop disabled with mpg seemingly improved on highway.
quote: Noticing some clutch slip at high boost after a summer of occasional pulls.
author: gtman

claim: A 2024 Sport hatch owner on KTuner base maps then Phearable Stage 2 with bad fuel and too much E85 burnt out the catalytic converter and raised knock control; transmission was at its limit.
quote: put in a combination of bad fuel and too much e85, burnt out cat and caused knock control
author: cueyo

claim: 2022 Sport Touring owner flexing: Starter 21 Dual 1 for winter and Dual 2 for summer; reports white smoke at WOT in 30F weather (likely moisture).
quote: Starter 21 (Dual 1 for winter and Dual 2 for summer)
author: johaw

claim: TSP Stage 1 on a Si: Map 3 target is 25 psi (KTuner map 3 is 23 psi); owners prefer KTuner map 3 for smoothness while TSP map 3 occasionally slipped the stock clutch.
quote: ktuner map 3(23psi) & Tsp 1 map 3(25psi)
author: jsocks014
